findings.description: Input size enforcement: Blob=[131072]byte is enforced at compile time by Go's static type system; no runtime check is needed or possible. A caller providing network/transaction data must deserialize it into the Blob type, and that deserialization step enforces the size constraint before ComputeCellsAndKZGProofs is ever called.

Output count enforcement: ckzg4844.ComputeCellsAndKZGProofs returns fixed-size [128]ckzg4844.Cell and [128]ckzg4844.KZGProof arrays. The slice conversion ckzgCells[:] produces a slice with len=cap=128. makeCellsAndProofs iterates all 128, producing exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB=128 cells and proofs on success.

Defensive guard in makeCellsAndProofs: the len(ckzgCells) != len(ckzgProofs) check is structurally redundant since both come from fixed [128]-element array slices, but harmless as belt-and-suspenders defense.

abstract_interpretation.summary: Trust boundary tb-001 is enforced at two levels: input size by Go's Blob=[131072]byte type at compile time, and output count by c-kzg-4844's fixed [128]Cell/[128]KZGProof return types at the C binding level. makeCellsAndProofs provides a redundant but harmless parity check.

symbolic_execution.summary: No code path allows a blob of non-BYTES_PER_BLOB size to reach the C library. Error paths return CellsAndProofs{} (zero value, no partial output), preventing callers from receiving partial or incorrect cell counts.

invariant_proving.summary: Two-layer formal proof: (1) Input invariant: Blob=[131072]byte statically enforces BYTES_PER_BLOB — proven by Go type system at compile time, not bypassable at runtime. (2) Output invariant: c-kzg-4844 returns [128]Cell and [128]KZGProof fixed arrays; slicing to []T preserves len=128; makeCellsAndProofs appends all 128 of each, producing exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB=128 in output. Both invariants hold for all non-error executions.

audit_items.summary: Trust boundary tb-001 is strictly enforced in Prysm's wrapper: BYTES_PER_BLOB input size is guaranteed by Go's compile-time type system (Blob=[131072]byte), and CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB output count is guaranteed by c-kzg-4844's fixed [128]Cell return type combined with makeCellsAndProofs faithfully converting all 128 elements. No enforcement gap exists. The redundant length check in makeCellsAndProofs is a harmless defensive guard.
recommendations: No action required. The trust boundary is correctly enforced through a combination of Go's static type system and c-kzg-4844's fixed-size return types.
The defensive len(ckzgCells) != len(ckzgProofs) check in makeCellsAndProofs can be retained as belt-and-suspenders; it is structurally impossible to trigger but documents intent clearly.

Ensure that all callers that accept blob data from external sources (network deserialization paths) correctly enforce the Blob=[131072]byte type constraint before passing data to ComputeCellsAndKZGProofs, as the trust boundary enforcement at the Go API level depends on correct upstream deserialization.

abstract_interpretation.summary: The notifyNewPayload function (lines 221-293) submits an ExecutionPayload to the execution engine via the engine_newPayloadVX JSON-RPC API. The ExecutionPayload protobuf definition does NOT contain an ommers or uncle_hash field — this field was removed from the EL payload format at The Merge (Bellatrix/EIP-3675). There is no abstract domain over ommers because ommers are structurally absent from the beacon block body and execution payload types used by Prysm. The Fulu/Fusaka fork introduces no new ommers-related fields.

symbolic_execution.summary: No path exists in notifyNewPayload (lines 221-293) that accepts or processes an ommers field. The ExecutionPayload variants in the Go protobuf-generated structs contain only standard post-merge fields (parent_hash, fee_recipient, state_root, transactions, withdrawals, etc.). Ommers were removed from the payload schema per EIP-3675. No counterexample can be constructed where Prysm's code passes non-empty ommers through.

invariant_proving.summary: The invariant holds by structural enforcement: (1) the ExecutionPayload protobuf has no ommers field (design-level exclusion since Bellatrix), (2) the engine_newPayloadVX API spec does not include ommers in any payload version, (3) the EL is the authoritative enforcer and returns INVALID for malformed blocks, and (4) Prysm correctly treats INVALID status as a fatal block error via invalidBlock{ErrInvalidPayload} at lines 284-289.

audit_items.summary: The property holds by design. The execution engine enforces the empty-ommers invariant at the EL level and returns INVALID status to Prysm if violated; Prysm correctly propagates this as block rejection via invalidBlock{ErrInvalidPayload} at lines 284-289 of execution_engine.go. There is no vulnerability in Prysm's implementation.
recommendations: No code changes required. The existing architecture correctly enforces the empty-ommers invariant through the Engine API protocol design and Prysm's INVALID-status handling.
This checklist item should be re-scoped or removed from future audit rounds as it tests an invariant enforced at the protocol/schema level rather than in Prysm's application code.

abstract_interpretation.summary: HashTreeRoot acquires a mutex lock, calls initializeMerkleLayers (idempotent; skips if merkleLayers already populated) then recomputeDirtyFields (iterates deterministic field enum set), returns merkleLayers[last][0] as 32-byte root. fieldRoots is a deterministic positionally-indexed slice produced by ComputeFieldRootsWithHasher. stateutil.Merkleize operates on a fixed-position slice with no map iteration over insertion-ordered collections, producing deterministic output.

symbolic_execution.summary: No counterexample possible: field indices are static enum constants with deterministic RealPosition() mapping; Merkleize pads to power-of-two with zero bytes and hashes pairs bottom-up. No ordering dependency on key insertion exists anywhere in the call chain.

invariant_proving.summary: PROOF HOLDS: field positions are compile-time constants (types.FieldIndex.RealPosition()); ComputeFieldRootsWithHasher returns a positionally-indexed slice; stateutil.Merkleize is a pure deterministic function. The mutex in HashTreeRoot prevents concurrent mutation during root computation. SSZ specification mandates determinism and this implementation faithfully enforces it.

audit_items.summary: SSZ HashTreeRoot is deterministic and order-independent by construction. Field positions are compile-time constants mapped via RealPosition(), and stateutil.Merkleize is a pure function operating on a positionally-indexed slice padded to a power-of-two. The mutex guard prevents concurrent mutation, and no ordering ambiguity exists. Property INV-020 holds provably.
recommendations: No remediation required. The SSZ HashTreeRoot implementation is provably deterministic.
Ensure that any future additions of new beacon state fields assign unique, static FieldIndex constants to preserve determinism.
